notes: Round 6 (security fix, ZB-PHO003-04, Kemi's architectural ruling): Zainab's round-5 finding was the third consecutive round narrowing the same underlying mistake - rounds 3-5 each tried to RECONSTRUCT 'did this exact attempt already promote' from BIO-PHO-001's own post-hoc state (content equality, then an exact attempt-id audit lookup, then a repository-existence confirmation), each fix closing one failure shape and immediately exposing an adjacent one, because PhotoMaster genuinely has no caller-supplied identity field and inferring ownership of an external side effect from that system's own observable state can never be fully disambiguated from outside it. god escalated to Kemi rather than dispatching a sixth reactive patch. Kemi's ruling: stop reconstructing, start REMEMBERING - the same category of fix as BIO-PHO-002's own TD-PHO-002-IDEMPOTENCY-RACE remediation, applied to an unrelated operation; PhotoQualityCapture.PendingApprovalAttemptId was already the right crash-survivable key, no new field needed anywhere. ApproveAsync now Claims that attempt id as a LOCAL idempotency key (a fresh, project-local IIdempotencyStore at api/features/bio-pho-003/Domain/IdempotencyStore.cs, the same copy-per-feature convention BIO-CRD-001/BIO-PHO-002 already established) BEFORE calling PromoteAsync: a genuine first attempt (IsNewClaim) promotes once and Completes the claim with the result; any resumed retry (same or a different authorized actor) finds the claim already Completed and returns its stored result directly - zero further calls to BIO-PHO-001 at all, no reconstruction, nothing left to misattribute. A genuinely failed promotion Releases its claim so a real retry can actually re-attempt rather than waiting out a pointless timeout. IPhotoMasterPromotionGateway shrinks back to exactly BIO-PHO-002's own shape - just PromoteAsync, nothing else; BIO-PHO-001's own module registration reverts to its original single-line IPhotoAuditSink form (the round-3/4 concrete-type registration this feature no longer needs is gone). Zero change to PhotoMaster, its repository, or any shared contract - no ADR needed. Named residual (Kemi's own ruling, disclosed and deliberately not chased further): a crash strictly between PromoteAsync succeeding and Complete() leaves that claim stuck InFlight forever in the volatile, process-lifetime store - a retry's own bounded poll-wait then times out and throws idempotency_wait_timeout (503) rather than silently reusing wrong data, the same 'crash residual inert with volatile singletons' boundary every in-memory placeholder in this codebase carries pending ADR-0005's real persistence - fails LOUD instead of today's SILENT wrong-photo risk, proven directly by a test reproducing exactly that window (claim the key, let the real promotion succeed, never call Complete, retry under a different operator times out rather than reusing anything). Verified by six PhotoQualityServiceTests replacing the round 3/4/5 reconstruction tests: crash before the marker (never promoted), a genuinely failed promotion whose claim is released so a real retry re-promotes, crash after promotion before audit (different-operator retry returns the Completed claim's stored result, still credited to the original actor), crash after audit before final commit (never re-promoted, never re-audited), the reject-in-progress refusal, and Kemi's own named residual. Feature unit tests 39/39 (net -2 vs round 5's 41, having removed 4 now-obsolete reconstruction tests and added 2 new idempotency-specific ones), full dotnet integration suite 250/250 (unaffected), dotnet unit suite 210/210 (unaffected), structural harness 55/55, tsc/next build/frontend vitest unaffected (no frontend changes this round). See docs/features/bio-pho-003/README.md's 'Security review round 1' section (ZB-PHO003-02 sub-section now covers all six rounds and Kemi's final ruling) for the full record.
